messages:
anna: quick ask — can someone run the miniheap-evict branch on a canary?
I keep seeing gradual RSS creep on smallalloc-heavy workloads after the kvcache prefix change. Not a full OOM yet but dangerous. @raj @sophia

raj: I can do a run later today. which benchmark should I use? the micro-alloc harness or the production-ish replay?

anna: start with micro-alloc (smallalloc-bench) to repro quickly, then repro with the replay if we see growth.
specifically: 64 concurrent workers, alloc sizes skewed to small (16-256B), live ratio ~0.6.

raj: got it. going to run: 
```
SERVICE=canary ./tools/run_smallalloc_bench --iters=6 --concurrency=64 --dist=small-heavy --live-ratio=0.6 
```
I'll export heapshots and full pprof if it bubbles.

derek: FYI saw two OOMs yesterday on a canary in eu-west-1 around 03:40 UTC. stack traces pointed to kvcache eviction path + allocator fragmentation. tagging in case the bench reproduces same pattern.

anna: thanks — if you have the OOM logs, drop them in the thread. even small snippets help.

derek: pasted the gist: <http://ci.internal/logs/oom-2034>
stack line: runtime/alloc.go:245 -> runtime/arena: alloc_chunk (approx). memory map showed a lot of small free extents.

raj: first micro run completed — no immediate crash but RSS drift of ~80MB over 10m. attached heapshot: <http://ci.internal/artifacts/heapshot/2045123456/1>
pprof shows many tiny free blocks in mini-arenas, fragmentation ratio ~1.37.

sophia: couple heuristics to try:
- enable more aggressive mini-heap compaction on free: set ENV REDWOOD_MINIHEAP_COMPACT=1 for the run.
- try jemalloc opt MALLOC_CONF: decay_time:1, lg_dirty_mult:0 (if using jemalloc)
- for our allocator, try bumping mini-evict threshold to 8MB (was 4MB) to force earlier consolidation.

anna: can you add the exact envs/flags we should use? I can queue a canary plan after.

sophia: try this set: 
```bash
export REDWOOD_MINIHEAP_COMPACT=1
export REDWOOD_MINIHEAP_EVICT_THRESHOLD=8388608  # 8MB
export MALLOC_CONF=lg_dirty_mult:0,decay_time:1
SERVICE=canary ./tools/run_smallalloc_bench --iters=6 --concurrency=64 --dist=small-heavy --live-ratio=0.6 
```
Also include --heapshot=on to write periodic snapshots.

raj: re-ran with those envs. RSS stabilized much better — drift down to ~10MB over same window. heapshot differences show fewer live tiny extents and more coalesced free regions. pushing artifacts: <http://ci.internal/artifacts/heapshot/2045123456/2>

derek: nice. can you also run a 30m replay with the real workload? fragmentation might behave differently under real request shapes.

raj: queuing a replay now; CI bot says estimate ~45m. starting run: <http://ci.internal/ci/2050/replay-queue/2045123456>

ci-bot: replay job queued — job id 2050. logs will be available at <http://ci.internal/ci/jobs/2050>. notify on completion. :robot_face:

anna: great progress. if the replay looks good, let's prepare a small canary rollout with REDWOOD_MINIHEAP_COMPACT enabled and the evict threshold bump. we'll monitor cost/latency and OOM rate.

sophia: and add a regression test to the perf suite: run_smallalloc_bench with the envs as part of presubmit so we catch future regressions.

raj: replay finished — no OOMs, RSS stable, latency percentiles unchanged. saving diff to the perf dashboard. <http://perf.internal/dash/miniheap/2045123456>

anna: fantastic. i'll draft the canary rollout plan and ping infra for the change. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
